items.q: Before diagnosing CKD on USG one must rule out hydronephroureteronephrosis, whose clue on imaging is:
opts: Calyces becoming prominent and ureter seen
items.exp: Rule out hydronephroureteronephrosis before diagnosing CKD; calyces becoming prominent and ureter seen. (Book p749)

items.q: Match each tempo with its non-CKD category — 1) Hours to days 2) Days to weeks 3) Normal RFT with renal disease … A) Acute kidney injury (AKI) B) Rapidly progressive renal failure (RPRF) C) Nephrotic syn / RTA type I-II / asymptomatic urine abnormality
items.exp: Hours to days → AKI; days to weeks → RPRF; normal RFT with renal disease → nephrotic syn, RTA I/II, asymptomatic urine abnormality. (Book p749)

items.q: The AKI arm of the flowchart lists postrenal, ATN, AIN and:
opts: Pre-renal investigation with normal urine analysis
items.exp: AKI: postrenal (B/L hydronephroureteronephrosis on USG), pre-renal (normal urine analysis), ATN, AIN. (Book p749)

items.q: Which statement about the AKI arm is TRUE?
opts: The pre-renal category is expected to show a normal urine analysis
The postrenal category shows a normal USG
ATN and AIN are postrenal causes
B/L hydronephroureteronephrosis defines the pre-renal category
items.exp: Pre-renal investigation: normal urine analysis; postrenal: B/L hydronephroureteronephrosis (USG). (Book p749)
